Today the condition is written twice (checklist_engine.py ~1731-1738 and ~1961-1966) in two functions with no call relationship; nothing fails if a later edit adds a condition to one and not the other, which would widen the exemption past what the engine actually instructs. Out of scope for epic-568-510 under its frozen pre-ruling 2.

Pre-existing #467 behaviour found while probing #510, unchanged by this diff and out of its scope: over the hard line, a start aimed at a gate id that does not exist writes a trip_ledger row for that nonexistent gate (gate: nope, outcome: begin-refused) and raises the trip refusal, shadowing the engine's own no such item error. The append-only ledger therefore accumulates rows for gates that were never in the checklist, and the agent is told to attach a refresh-request against an id that cannot hold one. Reproduced against BOTH the pre-change and post-change engine, so it belongs to #467, not #510.
